unit.input:
; TestCave_TwoFixed.svx -- dummy data for CsNetwork/CsAdjust testing:
; two fixed stations on ONE connected ring, plus a THIRD fixed station
; that anchors a separate, otherwise-disconnected component joined to
; the ring by exactly one leg. See Task 1d, docs/superpowers/plans/
; 2026-08-21-loop-closure-adjustment.md, for why three *fix stations
; are needed to realize the two required shapes (two fixed stations
; forming a two-root ring is one shape; a SEPARATELY fixed component
; tied on by a single bridge leg is the other, and that second
; component needs its own control to anchor itself before the tie is
; even meaningful to classify).
;
; All bearings are 0/90/180/270 and all lengths are integers so every
; expected number in tests/js_unit.js is exact arithmetic, not a
; calculator result.

*units length metres
*units compass degrees
*fix RA 0 0 0
*fix RC 10 10 0
*fix SB1 20 3 0
*data normal from to tape compass clino

; --- component A: a 4-leg ring, fixed at two opposite corners RA/RC.
; Surveyed exactly consistent with both fixed corners -- deliberately
; ZERO misclosure here, so the two arc-loops this produces (see the
; hand computation in tests/js_unit.js) are as clean as the existing
; synthetic "ring" fixture they mirror.
RA RB 10.00 0.00 0.00
RB RC 10.00 90.00 0.00
RC RD 10.00 180.00 0.00
RD RA 10.00 270.00 0.00

; --- the single bridge leg joining component A to component B. Walked
; from RD (10,0,0) east 10m lands at (20,0,0); SB1's own control is
; (20,3,0) -- a deliberate, exact 3m misclosure, so this leg is a
; control TIE, not a loop.
RD SB1 10.00 90.00 0.00

; --- component B: SB1 (fixed) plus one ordinary traversed station.
; Without the RD-SB1 leg above, this is a wholly separate component
; with its own anchor (SB1) -- exactly the "genuinely disconnected
; fixed component" shape Task 1d asks for.
SB1 SB2 10.00 0.00 0.00

; PitfallCave_Dialects.svx -- parser dialect traps, hand-written.
; Generated fixtures cannot carry these: a writer never emits them.
; Every block is annotated with what a reader gets WRONG if it
; mishandles the directive. Geometry is deliberately trivial (round
; bearings, whole numbers) so a wrong answer is obvious by eye.
;
; The cave itself is nonsense -- this file is about the directives.
; Note the SHAPE of the file: the unit and angle switches are FLAT
; inside one *begin block, because in real Survex a nested block
; renames its stations (prefix.name) and a leg written across the
; boundary is two different stations, not a connection. The one
; nested block below is deliberately a separate component with its
; own *fix -- which is also the prefix-naming and flag-scope trap.

*begin DIALECT
*units length feet
*units compass degrees
*units clino degrees
*fix E1 reference 0 0 812.40
*date 2026-07-04
*team "N. SCHONEGG" compass clino
*team "R. WEBB" tape
*data normal from to tape compass clino

; --- 1. *calibrate declination is a ZERO ERROR. Survex computes
; (reading - X), so the model declination is -X. A reader that ADDS
; it rotates the whole survey by 2X -- 8.5 degrees here, invisible
; unless something is georeferenced.
*calibrate declination 4.25
E1 E2 100.00 90.00 0.00

; --- 2. the modern *declination has the CONVENTIONAL sign (added).
; Same magnitude as above, opposite meaning: E2->E3 must end up 8.5
; degrees away from E1->E2 in the model, not on top of it.
*declination 4.25
E2 E3 100.00 90.00 0.00

; --- 3. plumbs. Compass omitted with "-" is legal on a plumbed leg;
; UP/DOWN/U/D/+V/-V and LEVEL are keywords, not numbers. A reader
; that parseFloats these gets 0 and flattens a pitch to level.
E3 E4 40.00 - DOWN
E4 E5 40.00 - UP
E5 E6 25.00 - +V
E6 E7 25.00 180.00 LEVEL

; --- 4. anonymous stations are SPLAYS: "." ".." "..." and the
; PocketTopo "-". A reader that treats these as real station names
; builds a station called ".." that every later splay collides with.
E7 .. 12.00 45.00 0.00
E7 .. 14.00 135.00 0.00
E7 . 9.00 225.00 -5.00
E7 - 11.00 315.00 5.00

; --- 5. *flags. duplicate excludes from LENGTH; surface excludes
; from length AND plot; "not" clears; *flags splay makes a NAMED
; station's shot a wall shot.
*flags duplicate
E7 E8 50.00 90.00 0.00
*flags not duplicate
*flags surface
E8 E9 60.00 90.00 0.00
*flags not surface
*flags splay
E9 E9S 15.00 0.00 0.00
*flags not splay

; --- 6. UNIT SWITCH MID-FILE. These legs are surveyed in METRES; the
; survey's working unit is already feet, so every distance here must
; be CONVERTED, not copied. A reader that copies refoots a metric
; run and shrinks it by 3.28 -- the silent-refooting bug the CSV
; rewrite existed to kill. 30.48 m is exactly 100 ft.
*date 2026-07-05
*team "K. AYERS" tape
*units length metres
E9 M1 30.48 90.00 0.00
M1 M2 30.48 0.00 0.00
*units length feet

; --- 7. yards, and a unit FACTOR. 1 yd = 0.9144 m, so 33.33 yd is
; ~100 ft; the factor form "*units length 2 feet" means every tape
; reading counts double, so 50.00 is 100 ft.
*units length yards
M2 Y1 33.33 180.00 0.00
*units length 2 feet
Y1 Y2 50.00 180.00 0.00
*units length feet

; --- 8. grads and percent. 400 grads = 360 degrees; a clino in
; percent is a TANGENT, not an angle (100 percent = 45 degrees).
; Reading either as degrees is a wrong cave that still plots.
*units compass grads
Y2 G1 40.00 100.00 0.00
*units compass degrees
*units clino percent
G1 G2 40.00 90.00 100.00
*units clino degrees

; --- 9. backsights, and the field-name aliases. length/bearing/
; gradient are the long names for tape/compass/clino; backbearing
; and backgradient carry the backsight. The first pair below
; disagrees by 6 degrees in compass, the second by 4 in clino, and
; both must reach the fs/bs check rather than being averaged away.
*data normal from to length bearing gradient backbearing backgradient
G2 K1 45.00 90.00 -5.00 276.00 5.00
K1 K2 45.00 180.00 -5.00 0.00 -1.00
*data normal from to tape compass clino

; --- 10. *data passage LRUD is per STATION, associated with the TO
; station, and "-" means NOT MEASURED (null), which is not zero.
; The first station's reading has no arriving shot to carry it and
; belongs in survey.startLrud.
*data passage station left right up down
E1 3.0 4.5 6.0 0.0
E2 5.0 5.0 9.0 1.0
E3 - - 12.0 -
E4 0.0 0.0 30.0 2.0
*data normal from to tape compass clino

; --- 11. a NESTED block: its stations are renamed DIALECT.SIDE.*, so
; a leg written to "E9" in here would NOT reach DIALECT.E9 -- it is a
; separate component, which is why it carries its own *fix. The flag
; set is saved at *begin and restored at *end: the surface flag below
; must NOT leak out to the legs that follow this block, or real
; passage silently drops out of the cave's total length.
*begin SIDE
*fix S1 300 300 1300
*flags surface
S1 S2 40.00 90.00 0.00
*end SIDE

; --- 12. two *date lines with NO leg between them, each with its own
; *team. This used to credit T. FIRST with J. PARK's trip: the
; previous crew was cleared only when a LEG had been recorded since
; the last *date, and here there is none between them. A change of
; DATE now clears the crew on its own, so the trip below must read
; J. PARK alone. (The *team line between the two dates is what makes
; this a real reproduction -- without it the earlier crew is already
; cleared by the leg above and the trap never fires.)
*date 2026-07-06
*team "T. FIRST" notes
*date 2026-07-07
*team "J. PARK" notes
K2 P1 20.00 270.00 0.00

*end DIALECT

; two fixed stations on ONE connected ring, plus a THIRD fixed station
; that anchors a separate, otherwise-disconnected component joined to
; the ring by exactly one leg. See Task 1d, docs/superpowers/plans/
; 2026-08-21-loop-closure-adjustment.md, for why three *fix stations
; are needed to realize the two required shapes (two fixed stations
; forming a two-root ring is one shape; a SEPARATELY fixed component
; tied on by a single bridge leg is the other, and that second
; component needs its own control to anchor itself before the tie is
; even meaningful to classify).

; expected number in tests/js_unit.js is exact arithmetic, not a
; calculator result.

*fix RC 10 10 0
*fix SB1 20 3 0

; ZERO misclosure here, so the two arc-loops this produces (see the

; Without the RD-SB1 leg above, this is a wholly separate component
